title: Teeth Kaomoji ▼ш▼: Copy & Paste Fang & Sharp Teeth Faces
meta_description: Copy and paste teeth kaomoji: sharp teeth like ▼ш▼ and (・ш・), cute fangs (˶˃⤙˂˶), gritted ▼皿▼, toothy grins (≧ᗜ≦) and chomping ᗧ···ᗣ text faces.
hero_tagline: Fangs, sharp shark teeth, gritted teeth and wide toothy grins drawn in text. Click a face and paste it anywhere.
intro: A teeth kaomoji swaps the usual mouth for a character with points or a grid. ш, a Cyrillic letter, looks like a row of sharp teeth, and with ▼ as eyes or brows above it the face turns menacing, close to the ギザ歯 (giza-ba) shark teeth of anime. ⤙ adds one small tooth at the corner of the mouth, the cute single fang Japanese calls 八重歯 (yaeba). 皿, a kanji for a dish, reads as clenched teeth, and 廿 or 甘 as a square grid of them. For a smile that simply shows teeth, ᗜ draws a wide open grin. Several of these characters come from less common scripts, so a few may show as boxes on older devices.

sections.label: Cute Fangs
sections.intro: The single ⤙ fang. ૮ ა are floppy ears and ฅ are paws, so many of these are puppies and kittens showing a tooth.

sections.label: Sharp Teeth
sections.intro: ш makes a full row of pointed teeth. Plain dot eyes look goofy; ▼ eyes look like a monster.

sections.label: Gritted Teeth
sections.intro: 皿 and 廿 draw teeth pressed together, for straining, holding back or grinding through something. Faces shouting with bared teeth are on the angry kaomoji page.

sections.label: Toothy Grins
sections.intro: ᗜ and ᐛ are Canadian Aboriginal syllabics shaped like an open, teeth-showing smile.

sections.label: Chomping
sections.intro: ᗧ is an open mouth mid-bite, best known as a Pac-Man shape, and ᗣ is the ghost being chased.

faq.q: What character makes the sharp teeth in ▼ш▼?
faq.a: ш is the Cyrillic letter sha, which has three upward points and reads as a row of sharp teeth. The ▼ on each side act as narrowed eyes or angry brows.

⤙ is an arrow-tail symbol used here as one small fang at the corner of the mouth. Japanese calls a visible single canine 八重歯 (yaeba) and treats it as cute, which is why these faces are soft rather than scary.

faq.q: Why do some teeth kaomoji show as boxes?
faq.a: Characters such as ⤙, ᗜ and ᗧ come from symbol and syllabics blocks that some older fonts do not include. Faces built from ш, 皿 and ▼ use more common characters and display on most devices.
